visibleText:

Ask a question about this ballot

Proposition 423: Vail Unified School District budget override continuation

Proposition 423 asks voters in Vail Unified School District No. 20 whether the district may continue to exceed its state revenue control limit by up to 12.5% per year, starting with fiscal year 2027/2028 and for the six fiscal years after that. According to the district's Notice of Election, that would put the budget about $5,102,762 above the alternate budget for 2027/2028, at an estimated continuation of $1.61 per $100 of secondary assessed valuation. The district's governing board adopted the resolution calling the election on June 2, 2026, and the special election is consolidated with the General Election on November 3, 2026. It is a yes/no question; the records here do not include arguments for or against, or any breakdown of how the money would be spent.

visibleText:

Ask a question about this ballot

Governor

For the November 3, 2026 general election, our records list four people on the ballot for Arizona Governor: Katie Hobbs (Democratic), Andy Biggs (Republican), Risa Lombardo (Green), and Teri Ann Hourihan (listed as No Labels). Eight people originally filed for the July 21 primary — in addition to Hobbs, Biggs, Lombardo and Hourihan, they were Republicans Ken Miceli, Scott Neely and David Schweikert, and Hugh Lytle of the Arizona Independent Party. The primary was canvassed August 6, but the Secretary of State has not yet published its official general-election candidate list, so the roster narrows to the nominees once that is posted. The filings do not state whether any candidate is the incumbent.
